findings.text: The first paragraph answers 'what is this' plainly. A newcomer learns in a few lines what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves ('AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable').
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title and almost all of the page are about another project, firstmate. A newcomer may think they are on the wrong site until they read the third paragraph, which explains that the page is a sample study.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / h1 of the same text

findings.text: The lede promises model attribution, a separate checker, cost, and a verdict. Yet this sample of Athena's output never says which models wrote or checked this study, what it cost, or what verdict it got. That would be the clearest proof of the pitch, and it is missing.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: the repo link, a clone command, prerequisites, `./setup.sh`, and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. A 'Next step' link near the top jumps straight to them, so the 'what do I do now' question is well answered.

The prerequisites do not say which operating systems are supported. They also do not say whether a Rust toolchain or a paid Claude account is needed, so a newcomer could get stuck partway through setup.
findings.source: Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code).

findings.text: This link in the header is aimed at the repository owner, not a visitor. To a newcomer, 'your decision' is confusing.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Tracing every statement to a claim and then to exact file lines at a fixed commit is easy to check. The 'Limits of this study' section openly says that nothing was run. Both build trust in what Athena produces.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: The glossary is thorough, but some terms are still undefined: 'captain-held inventory', 'endpoint', 'crewmates', 'wake'. 'Stale wake' is defined using the word 'wake' itself. A newcomer reading the firstmate detail will run into these.
findings.source: the report exists and its captain-held inventory is verified (t11 Guard); re-resolves its durable harness pin (c41); stale wake: A wake after which the agent inspects a worker…

findings.text: 'About this page' gives an internal detail (a repository folder) instead of telling the visitor anything useful, such as how to make a study like this one with Athena.
findings.source: This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.
